meta./en-gb/food/dishes/khao-soi/: Khao soi is the Chiang Mai curry noodle dish with egg noodles in coconut broth and a crispy noodle topping. Learn how to eat it, which meats are offered and how to add lime and side dishes.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/sai-ua/: Sai ua is a grilled northern Thai pork sausage with chilli and herbs. Find out how it tastes, how it differs from sai krok Isan and why it is not suitable if you do not eat pork.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/nam-prik-ong/: Nam prik ong is a northern Thai dipping sauce of tomato, minced pork and chilli, eaten with vegetables and sticky rice. See how to eat it and why a tomato sauce is not automatically vegetarian.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/mi-hokkien/: Mi hokkien is a Phuket noodle dish of thick yellow noodles stir-fried with seafood and sauce. Learn how it differs from mi hun, what else may go in and what to ask if you cannot eat seafood.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/mi-hun/: Mi hun is a Phuket dish of thin rice noodles known for its pork rib broth. Read how it differs from mi hokkien, how noodles and broth are served and what to ask if you avoid pork.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/o-aew/: O-aew is a cold Phuket dessert of jelly, sweet syrup and toppings on ice. Learn how to eat it, why it suits a hot day in the old town and what to ask about jelly and toppings you avoid.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/boat-noodles/: Boat noodles in Ayutthaya are noodles and meat served in broth, a famous meal between the ruins. Learn how to choose noodles, meat and bowl size, and what to ask if you avoid offal.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/river-prawns/: Grilled river prawns are a famous Ayutthaya dish to share with rice. Find out why the price depends on prawn size and selling unit, how to ask per prawn or by weight, and how to eat them.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/roti-sai-mai/: Roti sai mai is the Ayutthaya snack of thin roti wrapped around spun sugar. Learn how to wrap it yourself and adjust the sweetness, how it differs from ordinary roti and what green pandan roti is.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/som-tam/: Som tam is the Isan papaya salad pounded in a mortar with chilli and a sour dressing. Learn how it tastes, what pla ra is, how to order it less spicy and why it may not be vegetarian.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/larb/: Larb is the Isan minced meat salad with lime, herbs and toasted rice powder, eaten with sticky rice. Learn how it tastes, why you should ask for cooked meat and how it differs from northern larb.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/sai-krok-isan/: Sai krok Isan is a sour fermented sausage of pork and rice from Isan. Find out how it tastes, how it differs from northern sai ua and how to eat the raw chillies served with it.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/au-pla/: Au pla is a spicy, salty freshwater fish curry presented as a local dish of Khon Kaen. Learn how it differs from som tam and larb, what to ask about the fish and how to eat it with rice.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/hat-yai-chicken/: Hat Yai fried chicken comes with fried shallots and sticky rice. Find out how it tastes, how to eat the chicken and shallots together and why chicken alone does not mean a dish is halal.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/bak-kut-teh/: Bak kut teh is a pork rib soup with herbs and aromatics, a Chinese dish found in the Songkhla area and Hat Yai. Learn how it tastes and why it is not suitable if you avoid pork.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/roti/: Thai roti is a street snack of griddled dough with condensed milk or chocolate, sometimes with banana. Learn how to order it, how it differs from roti sai mai and what to ask about egg and milk.
meta./en-gb/food/dishes/watermelon-shake/: Nam taeng mo pan is the Thai watermelon shake blended with water and ice. Learn how it differs from watermelon juice, how to ask for less sugar or syrup and how to compare cup size and price.

meta./en-gb/food/fruits/mangosteen/: Mangosteen in Thailand: the main season from April to August, how to open the purple shell, how the white flesh tastes and why the kilo price is not the weight of the flesh you eat.

meta./en-gb/food/fruits/lychee/: Lychee in Thailand: harvest listed from April to June, how to peel and eat it, the hong huai and chakkraphat varieties, and how kilo prices differ from set packs of lychee.
meta./en-gb/food/fruits/longkong/: Longkong in Thailand: harvest listed from May to September, how it differs from longan, how to peel the segments and why a fruit name and bunch shape matter when you order.
